items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: So it just so happened that Pearl Bailey was living in Washington then... the manager very quickly got Pearl Bailey to come into the club... So Pearl came and she worked these two weeks.

ctx.x: Yet still, I kept my mouth shut. I had nothing to say, because I had nothing to talk about anyway. But at the same time, I would always come up and listen to him. So after... You know, guys just walked away from him. They called him all kinds of "old-time so-and-so's..." I was left standing there with him. So he said to me, "One of these days you're going to be a good pianist, because you listen." Well, I'd been going up there every day just listening to him because he played the piano, and every now and then…

At that particular time he had Pearl Bailey singing up there, and a couple of other girls. That was my job. I played the piano for them, and sang, and played a few little things that I knew myself. And then, when showtime came, it would feature Jelly Roll Morton, and he would sit down and play and talk to the people about New Orleans and all of that. I always wondered then why, being on U Street and everything,
